method: A duplex circuit needs two strands, one in each direction, so the planner first provisions pairs = ceil(circuits x (1000 + spare tenths of a percent) / 1000) and then strands = 2 x pairs. A trunk cable carries a fixed number of fibers, so trunks = ceil(strands / fibers) and the installed strand count is trunks x fibers; the difference between that and the required count is reported as unused strands, and strand utilisation is strands / installed. Connectors follow the same counts: each trunk terminates in one MPO connector at each end, giving 2 x trunks; each duplex pair is presented on one LC duplex adapter at each end, so the adapters equal the installed strand count and the LC connectors, one per strand end, are twice that. The planner also evaluates 8-, 12- and 24-fiber trunks for the same requirement and names a smaller-waste option when one exists, preferring the larger trunk on a tie because it needs fewer cables. Duplex circuits are whole numbers from 1 to 100,000, spare capacity is 0 to 100 percent with at most one decimal place, and the trunk must be 8, 12 or 24 fibers; blank, fractional, negative and out-of-range values are refused with the failing field named instead of being defaulted. This is planning arithmetic: the polarity method, cassette mapping, spare policy and the parts actually ordered stay with the cabling designer, so the page states no sources for them.
